thread.title: Peru has a GDP per capita of $6,046 per 2016 World Bank Data

author: No Guilt
title: Peru has a GDP per capita of $6,046 per 2016 World Bank Data
text:
Peru has a GDP per capita of $6,046 per 2016 World Bank Data . In 2017, the best coffee in the world came from Peru judged at the Global Specialty Coffee Expo in Seattle.
On a recent trip to South America, I saw business booming at Starbucks ( SBUX ) in Peru.

Peru is significantly below the world's average income and people were still paying the equivalent of $3 for a coffee. Sure, many were tourists from the U.S., Brazil, England but many were Peruvian as well. The country is one of the top 10 coffee producers in the world, and last year, they beat out Columbia to have the best quality coffee in the world. Surely, you can find better quality coffee (and cheaper) in Peru than Starbucks, yet there it has over 75 shops and is doing well. Why?
The answer: America

Dilly Dilly
People around the world think America is cool. Last Summer, I was in Eastern Europe and I'd see 7-10 people every single day wearing an American flag shirt. Our music and movies are exported globally. In many parts of the world, people can't afford a visit to New York, Los Angeles or Miami, but they can walk over to McDonald's ( MCD ) or Starbucks to get a taste. American brands are also viewed as quality, in Asia, Nike ( NKE ) and Apple ( AAPL ) are viewed as premium foreign brands and even status symbols. Americans see something made in Italy and instantly view it as quality, the rest of the world views American products much the same way.
